```{r}
format_p <- function(value) {
  case_when(
    is.na(value) ~ "—",
    value < 0.001 ~ formatC(value, format = "e", digits = 2),
    TRUE ~ formatC(value, format = "f", digits = 3)
  )
}

format_number <- function(value, digits = 2) {
  ifelse(
    is.finite(value),
    formatC(value, format = "f", digits = digits),
    "—"
  )
}

format_clock <- function(value) {
  output <- rep("—", length(value))
  finite <- is.finite(value)
  minutes <- round((value[finite] %% 24) * 60) %% (24 * 60)
  output[finite] <- sprintf("%02d:%02d", minutes %/% 60, minutes %% 60)
  output
}

format_estimate_ci <- function(
  estimate,
  conf_low,
  conf_high,
  unit,
  effect_type = "difference"
) {
  output <- rep("—", length(estimate))
  finite <- is.finite(estimate) & is.finite(conf_low) & is.finite(conf_high)
  clock <- finite & unit == "clock time" & effect_type == "mean"
  output[clock] <- paste0(
    format_clock(estimate[clock]),
    " [",
    format_clock(conf_low[clock]),
    "–",
    format_clock(conf_high[clock]),
    "]"
  )
  numeric <- finite & !clock
  suffix <- ifelse(
    unit[numeric] %in% c("h", "lx", "lx·h"),
    paste0(" ", unit[numeric]),
    ""
  )
  prefix <- ifelse(effect_type[numeric] %in% c("ratio", "odds_ratio"), "×", "")
  output[numeric] <- paste0(
    prefix,
    formatC(estimate[numeric], format = "f", digits = 2),
    " [",
    formatC(conf_low[numeric], format = "f", digits = 2),
    "–",
    formatC(conf_high[numeric], format = "f", digits = 2),
    "]",
    suffix
  )
  output
}

format_r2 <- function(estimate, conf_low, conf_high) {
  output <- rep("—", length(estimate))
  finite_estimate <- is.finite(estimate)
  finite_interval <- finite_estimate & is.finite(conf_low) & is.finite(conf_high)
  output[finite_estimate] <- paste0(
    formatC(100 * estimate[finite_estimate], format = "f", digits = 1),
    "%"
  )
  output[finite_interval] <- paste0(
    formatC(100 * estimate[finite_interval], format = "f", digits = 1),
    "% [",
    formatC(100 * conf_low[finite_interval], format = "f", digits = 1),
    "–",
    formatC(100 * conf_high[finite_interval], format = "f", digits = 1),
    "]"
  )
  output
}

h01_gt <- function(data, ...) {

    )
}
```

## Result in brief

The audited near-eye analysis retains the familiar 17-metric H01 package.
Each metric is fitted with its declared response family, participant-day
outcomes include a participant random intercept, and the four model-wide
questions—site, photoperiod, latitude, and same-frame site-versus-latitude
adequacy—are adjusted as four separate 17-test Benjamini–Hochberg families.

The response-family review changed only one metric: calendar-day cumulative
time below 10 lx melEDI before sleep now uses a Gaussian identity model and is
reported as an ordinary difference. The submitted-style Tweedie/log model was
retained for time below 1 lx melEDI during sleep, and the shifted-log Gaussian
model was retained for darkest-10-hour mean melEDI because no common
alternative cleared the predefined diagnostic rule in both data scenarios and
placements.

Separately, the current melanopic daylight efficacy ratio (MDER) is the
arithmetic mean of viable one-minute melEDI-to-illuminance ratios. The
submitted V0 result used a ratio of daily integrals, which weighted moments by
illuminance. The two MDER rows are therefore a transparent version comparison
between related but different estimands, not a like-for-like refit of one
unchanged outcome.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-h01-claim-summary
#| tbl-cap: "Numbers of metrics supported after correction in the submitted V0 analysis and the audited main near-eye analysis."

claim_summary |>
  transmute(
    Question = question_label,
    `V0 supported` = submitted_supported_n,
    `Audited supported` = current_supported_n,
    `Newly supported` = newly_supported_metrics,
    `No longer supported` = no_longer_supported_metrics
  ) |>
  h01_gt() |>
  cols_align("center", columns = c(`V0 supported`, `Audited supported`)) |>
  cols_width(
    Question ~ px(130),
    `V0 supported` ~ px(105),
    `Audited supported` ~ px(120),
    everything() ~ px(270)
  ) |>
  tab_source_note(
    md(
      "Support means *q* < 0.05 within the applicable 17-test vector-wide BH family."
    )
  )
```

Relative to V0, the current analysis additionally supports overall site
associations for time above 250 lx melEDI during wake, time below 10 lx melEDI
before sleep, and MDER; latitude associations for time above 250 lx melEDI
during wake and MDER; and a photoperiod association for the L10 midpoint. The
MDER comparison reflects the estimand change described above. These are
model-wide results, not nine separate site contrasts. The hierarchical site
comparisons appear only for the ten metrics whose overall site test is
supported.

## Response-family decision

The candidate comparison used the identical implementation and model rows for
the main and manuscript-prepared scenarios. Selection required the declared
hard screens, common diagnostics, and all inferential fits to pass; descriptive
random-site singularity was reported but was not allowed to redefine
inferential eligibility.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-h01-family-selection
#| tbl-cap: "Response-family decisions for the three metrics that reopened the post-bootstrap gate."

candidate_selection |>
  transmute(
    Metric = manuscript_name,
    `Selected family` = selected_candidate_label,
    `Current retained` = if_else(current_candidate_retained, "Yes", "No"),
    `Common diagnostic screen` = selected_common_diagnostic_status,
    Rationale = selection_reason
  ) |>
  h01_gt() |>
  cols_width(
    Metric ~ px(220),
    `Selected family` ~ px(180),
    `Current retained` ~ px(90),
    `Common diagnostic screen` ~ px(190),
    Rationale ~ px(430)
  ) |>
  tab_style(
    style = cell_text(weight = "bold"),
    locations = cells_body(columns = `Selected family`)
  ) |>
  tab_source_note(
    md(
      "The alternative was selected only when it performed better under the fixed diagnostic rule in all required data scenarios and placements."
    )
  )
```

![Diagnostic status of all candidate response families across the eight required H01 runs.](../../artifacts/10_figures/H01/response_family_candidates/H01_response_family_diagnostic_status.png){#fig-h01-family-diagnostics fig-alt="A faceted diagnostic status plot compares three candidate response families for darkest-10-hour mean melEDI, time below 10 lx melEDI before sleep, and time below 1 lx melEDI during sleep across both data scenarios, near-eye and chest placements, and all-available and paired samples. Only the identity-scale Gaussian model for pre-sleep time has no strong diagnostic warning in any run." width="90%"}

The selected pre-sleep Gaussian model converged in all eight required runs,
had no strong residual warning, and stayed inside the 24-hour physical bound.
For the main near-eye fit its residual-variance ratio was 1.66. The calendar-
day cumulative construct is not truncated: observations strictly above six
hours remain valid and are reported as an audit warning.

## Gate A and Gate B outcome checks

Gate A retains the calendar-day cumulative estimand for time below 10 lx
melEDI before sleep. A calendar date can legitimately contain parts of two
diary-defined three-hour pre-sleep intervals; therefore values are not capped
at three hours. Values strictly above six hours trigger review without being
removed or truncated.

Gate B retains a linear clock model. The primary conversion subtracts 24 hours
only from L10 midpoint values strictly later than 16:00; the noon cut is the
same-row, same-family sensitivity. These are bell-shaped linear responses in
the fitted range, so no circular model is introduced.

::: {#fig-h01-l10-gate layout-ncol=2}

![Primary strict-after-16:00 conversion.](../../artifacts/10_figures/H01/gates/H01_l10_midpoint_primary_16h_conversion_histogram.png){fig-alt="Histogram of the primary strict-after-16:00 L10 midpoint conversion. The distribution is unimodal and approximately bell-shaped on its linear scale, with the nighttime cluster away from the conversion cut."}

![Noon-cut sensitivity.](../../artifacts/10_figures/H01/gates/H01_l10_midpoint_noon_conversion_sensitivity_histogram.png){fig-alt="Histogram of the noon-cut L10 midpoint sensitivity using the same observations and model. The distribution remains a linear clock-time sensitivity rather than a circular response."}

Primary strict-after-16:00 conversion (left) and the predefined noon-cut
sensitivity (right).

:::

## Reconstructed Table S2

The submitted Table S2 combined model tests, fixed effects, nine site
deviations, and random-effect summaries in one very wide bitmap. The faithful
reconstruction below preserves its metric categories and questions but splits
the content into three semantic tables: model-wide tests, effect estimates,
and hierarchical site follow-ups. This allows 95% confidence intervals and
both raw and adjusted p-values to remain readable.

### Model-wide tests: audited analysis versus V0

```{r}
#| label: tbl-h01-s2-tests
#| tbl-cap: "Reconstructed Table S2A: model-wide tests in the audited main near-eye analysis and the submitted V0 analysis."

s2_tests <- model_overview |>
  arrange_h01_metrics() |>
  transmute(
    Category = recode(
      as.character(manuscript_category),
      !!!category_labels
    ),
    Metric = manuscript_name,
    `Site: audited` = paste0(
      "p=", format_p(site_p_raw), "; q=", format_p(site_p_adjusted)
    ),
    `Site: V0 q` = format_p(site_p_adjusted_v0),
    `Photoperiod: audited` = paste0(
      "p=", format_p(photoperiod_p_raw),
      "; q=", format_p(photoperiod_p_adjusted)
    ),
    `Photoperiod: V0 q` = format_p(photoperiod_p_adjusted_v0),
    `Latitude: audited` = paste0(
      "p=", format_p(latitude_p_raw),
      "; q=", format_p(latitude_p_adjusted)
    ),
    `Latitude: V0 q` = format_p(latitude_p_adjusted_v0),
    `Site vs latitude adequacy` = paste0(
      "p=", format_p(adequacy_p_raw),
      "; q=", format_p(adequacy_p_adjusted)
    )
  )

s2_tests |>
  h01_gt(groupname_col = "Category", rowname_col = "Metric") |>
  tab_spanner(
    label = "Overall site",
    columns = c(`Site: audited`, `Site: V0 q`)
  ) |>
  tab_spanner(
    label = "Photoperiod",
    columns = c(`Photoperiod: audited`, `Photoperiod: V0 q`)
  ) |>
  tab_spanner(
    label = "Latitude",
    columns = c(`Latitude: audited`, `Latitude: V0 q`)
  ) |>
  cols_label(
    `Site: audited` = "Audited p; q",
    `Site: V0 q` = "V0 q",
    `Photoperiod: audited` = "Audited p; q",
    `Photoperiod: V0 q` = "V0 q",
    `Latitude: audited` = "Audited p; q",
    `Latitude: V0 q` = "V0 q",
    `Site vs latitude adequacy` = "Site vs latitude p; q"
  ) |>
  cols_align("center", columns = -Metric) |>
  cols_width(
    Metric ~ px(260),
    everything() ~ px(128)
  ) |>
  tab_source_note(
    md(
      "Each audited q-value belongs to one complete 17-test BH family. V0 columns reproduce the submitted adjusted values; V0 did not report the same-frame adequacy family."
    )
  )
```

```{r}
  transmute(

s2_effects |>

    everything() ~ px(95)

  tab_source_note(

    )

```

### Hierarchical site follow-ups

Only metrics with a supported overall site test enter this table. Every row is
a comparison of one site with the equally weighted overall site mean. The raw
p-value and the BH-adjusted p-value across the nine site comparisons for that
metric are both shown.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-h01-site-followups
#| tbl-cap: "Hierarchical site comparisons with the equally weighted overall site mean for metrics with a supported overall site test."

site_display <- site_followups |>
  mutate(
    Category = recode(manuscript_category, !!!category_labels),
    Metric = manuscript_name,
    Site = site_display_name,
    `Effect [95% CI]` = format_estimate_ci(
      estimate_practical,
      conf_low_practical,
      conf_high_practical,
      if_else(display_unit == "clock time", "h", display_unit),
      effect_type
    ),
    `Raw p` = format_p(p_raw),
    `Within-metric q` = format_p(p_adjusted_within_metric),
    `Overall site q` = format_p(overall_site_p_adjusted),
    metric_group = paste0(Category, " — ", Metric)
  ) |>
  arrange(metric_order, display_order) |>
  select(
    metric_group,
    site,
    Site,
    `Effect [95% CI]`,
    `Raw p`,
    `Within-metric q`,
    `Overall site q`
  )

site_gt <- site_display |>
  h01_gt(groupname_col = "metric_group") |>
  cols_hide(columns = site) |>
  cols_align(
    "center",
    columns = c(`Effect [95% CI]`, `Raw p`, `Within-metric q`, `Overall site q`)
  ) |>
  cols_width(
    Site ~ px(165),
    `Effect [95% CI]` ~ px(220),
    everything() ~ px(120)
  )

for (site_code in unique(site_display$site)) {
  site_color <- site_followups$site_color[
    match(site_code, site_followups$site)
  ]
  site_gt <- site_gt |>
    tab_style(
      style = list(
        cell_fill(color = site_color, alpha = 0.22),
        cell_text(weight = "bold")
      ),
      locations = cells_body(columns = Site, rows = site == site_code)
    )
}

site_gt |>
  tab_source_note(
    md(
      "Site names, visible order, and colours follow DISPLAY-001. The three German sites intentionally share the registered colour; their text labels distinguish them."
    )
  )
```

## Reconstructed Table S3: variation represented

Marginal R² represents the complete fixed-effect set; conditional R² represents
fixed and participant random effects together. The participant-associated
share is conditional minus marginal R² for participant-day models. Site and
photoperiod part R² values are term-specific reductions in fixed-effect
prediction variance and are deliberately not added because their information
can overlap. Latitude part R² belongs to the separate latitude model.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-h01-s3-r2
#| tbl-cap: "Reconstructed Table S3: audited R² and part-R² summaries with 95% joint-bootstrap intervals."

r2_display <- r2_preview |>
  mutate(
    category_sort = if_else(metric_order == 0, -1, match(manuscript_category, category_order)),
    Category = if_else(
      metric_order == 0,
      "Grand average",
      recode(manuscript_category, !!!category_labels)
    ),
    Metric = if_else(
      preview_only & metric_order > 0,
      paste0(manuscript_name, " †"),
      manuscript_name
    ),
    `Model R²` = format_r2(
      conditional_r2_estimate,
      conditional_r2_conf_low,
      conditional_r2_conf_high
    ),
    `Fixed effects R²` = format_r2(
      marginal_r2_estimate,
      marginal_r2_conf_low,
      marginal_r2_conf_high
    ),
    `Site part R²` = format_r2(
      site_part_r2_estimate,
      site_part_r2_conf_low,
      site_part_r2_conf_high
    ),
    `Photoperiod part R²` = format_r2(
      photoperiod_part_r2_estimate,
      photoperiod_part_r2_conf_low,
      photoperiod_part_r2_conf_high
    ),
    `Latitude part R²` = format_r2(
      latitude_part_r2_estimate,
      latitude_part_r2_conf_low,
      latitude_part_r2_conf_high
    ),
    `Participant-associated` = format_r2(
      participant_associated_share_estimate,
      participant_associated_share_conf_low,
      participant_associated_share_conf_high
    ),
    `Not represented` = format_r2(
      unrepresented_share_estimate,
      unrepresented_share_conf_low,
      unrepresented_share_conf_high
    ),
    `Bootstrap evidence` = case_when(
      metric_order == 0 & preview_only ~ "Preview mean",
      metric_order == 0 ~ "Descriptive mean",
      preview_only ~ "PILOT: 50",
      TRUE ~ "Production: 1,000"
    )
  ) |>
  arrange(category_sort, metric_order) |>
  select(
    Category,
    Metric,
    `Model R²`,
    `Fixed effects R²`,
    `Site part R²`,
    `Photoperiod part R²`,
    `Latitude part R²`,
    `Participant-associated`,
    `Not represented`,
    `Bootstrap evidence`
  )

r2_gt <- r2_display |>
  h01_gt(groupname_col = "Category", rowname_col = "Metric") |>
  tab_spanner(
    label = "Complete model",
    columns = c(`Model R²`, `Fixed effects R²`)
  ) |>
  tab_spanner(
    label = "Non-additive term summaries",
    columns = c(`Site part R²`, `Photoperiod part R²`, `Latitude part R²`)
  ) |>
  cols_align("center", columns = -Metric) |>
  cols_width(
    Metric ~ px(245),
    everything() ~ px(145)
  ) |>
  tab_source_note(
    md(if (preview_active) {
      paste0(
        "Values are percentages with 95% percentile intervals. The grand ",
        "average is descriptive and has no interval. † PILOT — NOT FOR ",
        "INFERENCE OR MANUSCRIPT REPORTING."
      )
    } else {
      paste0(
        "Values are percentages with 95% percentile intervals from 1,000 ",
        "successful joint bootstrap refits per target. The grand average is ",
        "descriptive and has no interval."
      )
    })
  )

if (preview_active) {
  r2_gt <- r2_gt |>
    tab_style(
      style = list(
        cell_fill(color = "#FFF2CC"),
        cell_text(weight = "bold")
      ),
      locations = cells_body(
        rows = grepl("†$", Metric) | `Bootstrap evidence` == "Preview mean"
      )
    )
}
r2_gt
```

## Exact fitted samples

Every model reports its exact participants, participant-days, observations,
sites, and main-data measurement support where the metric producer retained
exact support minutes. Participant-level IS and IV have one model observation
per participant but retain the contributing participant-day count. In the main
data, exact support hours are unavailable only for the M10 and L10 mean and
midpoint metrics because their producer did not export exact support minutes;
they are not imputed. The manuscript-prepared sensitivity lacks reconstructable
metric-specific support records for every metric, so all of its support hours
remain explicitly unavailable.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-h01-exact-samples
#| tbl-cap: "Exact fitted samples for the main and manuscript-prepared near-eye scenarios."

exact_samples |>
  mutate(
    Scenario = data_scenario,
    Metric = manuscript_name,
    `Analysis unit` = if_else(
      analysis_unit == "participant_day",
      "Participant-day",
      "Participant"
    ),
    `Support hours` = if_else(
      derivation_support_status == "available",
      formatC(derivation_support_hours, format = "f", digits = 1),
      if_else(
        data_scenario_id == "main",
        "Unavailable*",
        "Unavailable†"
      )
    )
  ) |>
  arrange(Scenario, metric_order) |>
  select(
    Scenario,
    Metric,
    `Analysis unit`,
    Participants = participants,
    `Participant-days` = participant_days,
    Observations = observations,
    Sites = sites,
    `Support hours`
  ) |>
  h01_gt(groupname_col = "Scenario", rowname_col = "Metric") |>
  fmt_integer(columns = c(Participants, `Participant-days`, Observations, Sites)) |>
  cols_align(
    "center",
    columns = c(
      `Analysis unit`,
      Participants,
      `Participant-days`,
      Observations,
      Sites,
      `Support hours`
    )
  ) |>
  cols_width(Metric ~ px(280), everything() ~ px(115)) |>
  tab_source_note(
    md(
      "Support hours are derivation support, not additional model observations. * Main M10/L10 producer did not export exact support minutes. † Manuscript-prepared support records are unavailable. Neither is imputed."
    )
  )
```

## Sensitivity and complementary analyses

The identical implementation is applied to the manuscript-prepared data.
Near-eye remains primary, paired/common-sample analyses separate placement
from availability, and chest remains complementary rather than pooled. The
table summarizes how many of the 17 metrics are supported in each declared
family; the full metric-level p-values remain in the linked source CSV.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-h01-sensitivity-support
#| tbl-cap: "Supported metrics in each 17-test BH family across all declared data, placement, and common-sample runs."

run_order <- c(
  "Main near-eye — primary",
  "Main near-eye — paired/common sample",
  "Main chest — complementary",
  "Main chest — paired/common sample",
  "Manuscript-prepared near-eye — sensitivity",
  "Manuscript-prepared near-eye — paired/common sample",
  "Manuscript-prepared chest — complementary",
  "Manuscript-prepared chest — paired/common sample"
)

scenario_support |>
  mutate(
    run_label = factor(run_label, levels = run_order),
    display = paste0(supported_metrics, " / ", tests)
  ) |>
  select(run_label, family_label, display) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = family_label, values_from = display) |>
  arrange(run_label) |>
  rename(Run = run_label) |>
  h01_gt() |>
  cols_align("center", columns = -Run) |>
  cols_width(Run ~ px(320), everything() ~ px(175)) |>
  tab_source_note(
    md(
      "Cells show supported metrics / 17. The table reports stability of model-wide support, not similarity of effect magnitude."
    )
  )
```

Additional required checks are retained outside the four primary families:
the noon-cut L10 analysis uses the same rows and Gaussian model, the longest-
period analysis is repeated using only exactly identified bouts, latitude is
refitted after omitting each site in turn, and participant influence is
assessed by leave-one-participant-out refits. These sensitivity p-values do not
enter the primary multiplicity families.

## Figure S10: photoperiod and latitude

The reconstruction applies the submitted Figure S10 visual grammar to the new
audited data: the original square layout, density ridges, vertically jittered
points, black masks outside the theoretical civil-photoperiod envelope,
in-panel legend, and white annotation are retained. The registered site order,
names, and colours are unchanged. All points use the submitted circular
symbol; sites sharing a colour remain distinguishable by their fixed
north-to-south placement. The coloured observations and density ribbons are
drawn in front of the black impossible-photoperiod masks.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-h01-bootstrap-pilot

bootstrap_execution <- bind_rows(

)

bootstrap_execution |>
  h01_gt() |>

    columns = c(

  ) |>
  cols_width(
    Status ~ px(250),
    Checkpoint ~ px(240),
    everything() ~ px(105)
  ) |>
  tab_style(
    style = list(
      cell_fill(color = "#FFF2CC"),
      cell_text(weight = "bold")
    ),
    locations = cells_body(columns = Status, rows = Stage == "Pilot")
  ) |>
  tab_style(
    style = list(
      cell_fill(color = "#D9EAD3"),
      cell_text(weight = "bold")
    ),
    locations = cells_body(columns = Status, rows = Stage == "Production")
  ) |>

    )

```

The pilot used four parallel workers, one BLAS/OpenMP thread per worker, wrote
all eight completed target checkpoints, and produced no failed or warning
refit. The subsequently approved production run completed all eight changed
targets in 310.9 seconds. Of 12,000 attempted refits, 11,996 succeeded and
8,000 were retained; four failed attempts were replaced before each target
reached 1,000 successful joint refits. All 120 unchanged target draw hashes
remained unchanged.

The separately approved MDER production run completed its eight affected
targets in `r formatC(mder_production$target_wall_seconds, format = "f", digits = 1)`
seconds. Of `r format(mder_production$total_attempted_refits, big.mark = ",")`
attempted refits, `r format(mder_production$total_successful_refits, big.mark = ",")`
succeeded and `r format(mder_production$total_used_refits, big.mark = ",")`
were retained. The two failed warning attempts were excluded before every
target reached 1,000 successful joint refits. The focused verifier passed,
and no support disposition changed from the accepted MDER point-result gate.

## Claim consequences and unresolved items

The submitted broad conclusion that site differences are concentrated in
level- and timing-based outcomes remains recognizable, but it needs revision:
the audited analysis additionally supports an overall site effect for time
above 250 lx melEDI during wake, time below 10 lx melEDI before sleep, and the
current MDER. Time above 250 lx melEDI during wake and MDER also gain support
for latitude gradients. Photoperiod remains widely associated with duration,
level, dose, spectrum, and selected timing metrics, and the L10 midpoint joins
the supported photoperiod set. First light timing above 250 lx melEDI remains
unsupported for site. The MDER differences must be interpreted in light of
its changed estimand rather than as a pure implementation correction.

The site-versus-latitude adequacy family is new and must not be equated with a
separate residual site effect after latitude adjustment. Site and latitude are
competing fixed-effect representations of the same site-level structure in
identical model frames.

The submitted R² percentages cannot be carried forward as additive variance
contributions. The repaired marginal, conditional, participant-associated,
and term-level part-R² summaries remain separate; site and photoperiod part R²
are not summed. No response-family or bootstrap major-change gate remains
open. Diagnostic `WARN_REVIEW` rows remain visible for model-level review and
do not silently redefine the approved response families.

## Reproducibility and source data

The reporting layer reads only audited upstream R objects. It does not refit
models during rendering. Publication tables use `gt`, Quarto owns their labels
and captions, and every plotted figure has paired CSV source data.

The bounded numerical-zero amendment for darkest-10-hour mean melEDI replaced
only four primary L10 branches. Each branch has 1,000 retained successful joint
bootstrap refits. The focused verifier found no change in multiplicity support,
diagnostic disposition, sensitivity classification, or claim disposition; the
other 16 metrics and all gap-timing-unaware L10 outputs remain preserved.
